intervals.note: The official DOE page gives the opening year (1999). An earlier version of this record used 2011 (EXO-200 beginning operations there) as a lower bound because no opening date had been read; the cited quote was a depth statement, not an opening date.

name: Waste Isolation Pilot Plant
notes: WIPP is primarily a U.S. Department of Energy transuranic nuclear-waste repository; it hosted the EXO-200 double-beta-decay experiment as a secondary underground physics use. The official DOE page gives the facility's opening year (1999); see the interval's note.

depth.note: Converted from the quoted feet figure (2150 ft x 0.3048 = 655.3 m).
depth.quote: Transuranic waste is disposed of 2,150 feet underground in rooms mined from the salt bed.

summary.plain: An underground salt-bed site in New Mexico built by the U.S. Department of Energy to store nuclear waste. Its deep, quiet tunnels also hosted the EXO-200 physics experiment from 2011 to 2018.
summary.technical: DOE transuranic-waste geologic repository in a salt bed near Carlsbad, New Mexico, with storage rooms ~2150 ft (655 m) underground; hosted the EXO-200 136Xe double-beta-decay detector from 2011 to 2018.
